input.strategy_title: AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement for serving and training
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Two strategic customers are standardizing on AMD Instinct accelerators and need
RHOAI to serve and train on ROCm. Upstream vLLM and PyTorch both publish ROCm
support, but the platform ships only CUDA runtime builds, and we have no
first-hand data on functional or performance parity for our supported model
set. Feature and performance validation requires physical AMD GPU hardware —
none exists in our CI fleet today — and upstream ROCm image cadence is
controlled by AMD and the upstream communities.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the models the validation campaign clears. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Serving Runtimes
- Training Operator
- Distributed Workloads

## Out of Scope

- Intel Gaudi or other non-AMD accelerator families
- AMD GPU sharing/partitioning support

## Open Questions

1. Hardware access: the validation campaign (HLR-1) needs dedicated AMD
   Instinct nodes — procurement or partner-lab access is unresolved.
2. Upstream ROCm build cadence: whether AMD's runtime image releases align
   with our release trains is outside our control.

# AMD Instinct ROCm vLLM serving validation campaign

## Description

This investigation resolves the strategy's core unknown: whether vLLM serving
on AMD Instinct accelerators via ROCm achieves functional and performance
parity with the productized CUDA builds for the platform's supported model
set. It runs a validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware and
produces the per-model go/no-go scope that determines what gets productized.
Until this question is answered, the productization work cannot be scoped.

## Scope

- Stand up a validation environment on dedicated AMD Instinct nodes with the
  upstream ROCm runtime images and vLLM ROCm builds as published upstream.
- Execute functional validation of vLLM serving for every model in the
  supported model set, recording pass/fail per model.
- Execute performance validation (serving throughput and latency) per model
  against the CUDA baseline, using the platform's standard benchmark
  methodology.
- Validate that vLLM ROCm runtimes deploy and serve through the standard
  KServe InferenceService path on AMD Instinct nodes (KServe requires no code
  change; this confirms it keeps working).
- Produce the campaign report: per-model functional results, performance
  parity data, and a per-model go/no-go recommendation constituting the
  productization scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the supported model set, when each model is served with vLLM on ROCm
  on AMD Instinct hardware, then a functional pass/fail result is recorded
  for every model in the set.
- Given the functional results, when serving throughput and latency are
  measured, then performance parity data relative to the CUDA baseline is
  recorded per model.
- Given vLLM ROCm runtimes, when they are deployed as KServe
  InferenceServices on AMD Instinct nodes, then deployment and inference
  succeed through the standard serving path (KServe keep-working validation).
- Given the collected data, when the campaign concludes, then a published
  report states a go/no-go recommendation per model, defining the
  productization scope for the serving runtime.

## Risks

- Hardware access: dedicated AMD Instinct nodes must be secured via
  procurement or a partner lab; this availability precondition is
  externally controlled and gates campaign execution, not campaign design.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)** — full coverage: the campaign on physical AMD Instinct
  hardware establishes the functional and performance parity data for vLLM
  serving of the supported model set and produces the go/no-go scope for
  productization.

# Productized vLLM ROCm serving runtime for validated models

## Description

This epic productizes a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime for exactly the
models the validation campaign clears, turning the go/no-go scope into a
shippable platform capability. It extends the existing vLLM runtime
productization path (which today ships only CUDA builds) with a ROCm image
build and the corresponding serving runtime definition, so RHOAI can serve
the cleared models on AMD Instinct accelerators.

## Scope

- Add a ROCm build variant of the vLLM serving runtime image to the existing
  midstream build and release process, based on the upstream ROCm support
  already published by vLLM.
- Define the serving runtime resource (ServingRuntime/ClusterServingRuntime)
  that makes the ROCm runtime available for InferenceServices, scoped to the
  model list cleared by the validation campaign.
- Verify end-to-end serving of cleared models on AMD Instinct nodes through
  the standard KServe InferenceService path.
- Record the support scope: the runtime is supported for exactly the cleared
  model list on the validated AMD hardware.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the model list cleared by the validation campaign, when the ROCm
  runtime image is built, then the build completes green in the existing
  Konflux build pipeline.
- Given the built image, when the serving runtime resource is applied, then
  the ROCm runtime is selectable for InferenceServices platform-wide.
- Given the productized runtime, when an InferenceService serving a cleared
  model runs on AMD Instinct nodes, then inference requests succeed
  end-to-end through the standard serving path.
- Given the productization, when the support scope is stated, then it covers
  exactly the models cleared by the campaign and the validated AMD hardware.

## Risks

- Upstream ROCm image cadence is controlled by AMD and the upstream
  communities; base-image availability may not align with platform release
  trains. Tiered delivery: the validation campaign and training-side work
  deliver value independently of this epic's timing.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)** — full coverage: a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is
  productized for the models the validation campaign clears.

# Kueue amd.com/gpu quota handling and PyTorch ROCm training support

## Description

This epic makes PyTorch training on ROCm a supported capability: single- and
multi-GPU PyTorch jobs running on AMD Instinct accelerators are admitted
through Kueue with correct amd.com/gpu quota handling. It extends the
existing queueing and quota configuration (which today handles NVIDIA GPUs)
to the AMD resource name and validates the full training path end to end.

## Scope

- Configure Kueue quota handling for the amd.com/gpu resource name
  (ClusterQueue/LocalQueue resource flavors) so jobs requesting AMD GPUs are
  admitted with correct quota accounting and all-or-nothing (gang) semantics
  for multi-GPU topologies.
- Validate single-GPU and multi-GPU PyTorch training jobs on ROCm hardware,
  submitted as PyTorchJobs and admitted through Kueue (the Training Operator
  requires no code change; this confirms it keeps working on AMD nodes).
- Document the validated job shapes (single- and multi-GPU) and any driver
  prerequisites discovered, as input to the platform documentation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a ClusterQueue configured for amd.com/gpu, when a PyTorchJob
  requesting AMD GPUs is submitted, then it is admitted with correct quota
  accounting against the amd.com/gpu resource.
- Given a multi-GPU PyTorchJob on ROCm, when it is admitted, then it receives
  its full GPU allocation as an all-or-nothing admission (no partial
  topologies start).
- Given single-GPU and multi-GPU PyTorch training jobs using ROCm images,
  when they run on AMD Instinct nodes after Kueue admission, then the
  training jobs complete successfully (Training Operator keep-working
  validation).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1)** — full coverage: PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for
  single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota
  handling.

# AMD ROCm enablement documentation

## Description

This epic documents the AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement for the platform: the
supported AMD hardware, the driver prerequisites, the validated model list
for vLLM serving on ROCm, and the setup required for ROCm training with
Kueue quota. It is authored after the serving runtime productization and the
training support land, so the content states what was actually built and
validated.

## Scope

Content outline:

- **Supported AMD hardware** — the AMD Instinct accelerators validated by
  the campaign, and what is explicitly not supported (other accelerator
  families, GPU sharing/partitioning per the strategy's out-of-scope list).
- **Driver prerequisites** — the AMD driver and ROCm runtime prerequisites
  for serving and training nodes.
- **Validated model list** — the models cleared by the validation campaign,
  matching the productized serving runtime's support scope exactly.
- **Serving on ROCm** — how to deploy the ROCm vLLM serving runtime for the
  validated models.
- **Training on ROCm** — how to submit single- and multi-GPU PyTorch jobs on
  AMD accelerators, including Kueue queue setup for amd.com/gpu quota.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the productized ROCm serving runtime, when the documentation is
  published, then it states the supported AMD hardware, the driver
  prerequisites, and the validated model list matching the runtime's support
  scope.
- Given the training support, when the documentation is published, then it
  describes submitting single- and multi-GPU PyTorch jobs through Kueue with
  amd.com/gpu quota.
- Given the drafted content, when technical review completes, then the
  documentation has been technically reviewed against the implemented
  runtimes and quota configuration, with the review sign-off recorded.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)** — full coverage: documentation states supported AMD
  hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9020 (AMD GPU / ROCm enablement for serving and training)

Strategy spans four components, two owning teams (RHOAI Serving, Distributed
Workloads), and HLRs from P0 to P2, anchored by a hardware validation campaign
whose outcome gates productization scope — not below-threshold and not
docs-only, so the full decomposition path applies.

## Epic List

| Epic | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|------|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9020-E001 | AMD Instinct ROCm vLLM serving validation campaign | Investigation | RHOAI Serving | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9020-E002 | Productized vLLM ROCm serving runtime for validated models | Implementation | RHOAI Serving | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9020-E003 | Kueue amd.com/gpu quota handling and PyTorch ROCm training support | Implementation | Distributed Workloads | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9020-E004 | AMD ROCm enablement documentation | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Documentation | P1 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001["E001 ROCm serving validation campaign (Investigation)"] --> E002["E002 vLLM ROCm runtime productization"]
    E002 --> E004["E004 AMD enablement documentation"]
    E003["E003 Kueue amd.com/gpu training support"] --> E004
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 3 (Investigation gates downstream Implementation) | The campaign's go/no-go output determines which models the productized ROCm runtime must support — the scope of the downstream implementation. The outcome is a per-model list (not ≤3 bounded alternatives), so no conditional branch epics; the gate is recorded via `gated_by` with `rewrite` impact on the productization epic. |
| E002 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs-authoring blocked by all Implementations) | Documentation must state the validated model list and the runtime's support scope, which only exist once productization lands. |
| E003 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs-authoring blocked by all Implementations) | Documentation must state the training quota setup and driver prerequisites validated by the training work. |
| E001 ∥ E003 | Rule 14 (parallel) | Different components, different teams, no shared artifacts. Training support does not build on the serving campaign's outcome; both run concurrently. |

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Requirement | Epic |
|-----|----------|-------------|------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization. | RHAISTRAT-9020-E001 |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the models the validation campaign clears. | RHAISTRAT-9020-E002 |
| HLR-3 | P1 | PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling. | RHAISTRAT-9020-E003 |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list. | RHAISTRAT-9020-E004 |

Every HLR maps to exactly one epic; no orphaned requirements and no
priority-split candidates — each HLR is a distinct capability on a distinct
surface, and none is a restatement of another.

## Health Warnings

- **Missing strategy sections**: the strategy has no Impacted Teams table,
  Dependencies table, Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, or NFRs. Teams were
  taken from the architecture-context owning-team fields and acceptance
  criteria were derived from the HLR text; a reviewer may want the strategy
  backfilled.
- **Hardware access (open question 1)**: procurement or partner-lab access to
  dedicated AMD Instinct nodes is unresolved. This is an externally-controlled
  availability precondition, not an acceptance criterion and not an
  Investigation — its resolution does not change which epics exist or what
  they do, only when the campaign can execute. Recorded as a risk on the
  campaign epic.
- **Upstream ROCm build cadence (open question 2)**: AMD's runtime image
  release cadence is outside our control and may not align with release
  trains. Handled via tiered delivery (below) and recorded as a risk on the
  productization epic.
- **Passive components**: KServe needs no code change for ROCm (it is
  accelerator-agnostic per architecture context); its keep-working validation
  under AMD nodes is an acceptance criterion on the validation campaign,
  owned by the same team. Training Operator likewise needs no code change;
  its validation is an acceptance criterion on the training epic, owned by
  the same team.
- **Component mapping note**: the training epic spans two strategy components
  — Distributed Workloads (active: Kueue quota handling for amd.com/gpu) and
  Training Operator (passive: validation only). It is assigned the single
  canonical component "Distributed Workloads" as the most-relevant name; the
  Training Operator validation is carried as an acceptance criterion rather
  than a separate epic because the same team owns both.
- **Planning note (epic size)**: the validation campaign epic will likely run
  above the ~2-week guideline in calendar time — it covers the full supported
  model set plus hardware access lead time. Kept as one logical change: a
  single campaign against one hardware allocation; a split would duplicate
  the rig setup, environment bring-up, and hardware booking.
  **Re-split trigger**: re-split the campaign into per-model-family batches
  if the model set grows beyond what one lab engagement can cover or the
  execution effort exceeds a sprint of measured runtime.

## Tiered Delivery

The external dependency (AMD / upstream ROCm image release cadence, timing
uncertain) permits partial value before productization:

- **Tier 1 (independent value)**: the validation campaign (risk-reduction —
  consumes upstream ROCm images as-is and produces the parity data set) and
  the Kueue amd.com/gpu training support (independent user-facing value on
  the training side).
- **Tier 2 (gated)**: the vLLM ROCm serving runtime productization, gated by
  the campaign's go/no-go scope; its timing additionally tracks upstream ROCm
  image availability for the chosen base.
